card.name: Subject right before past-tense 'would/was to'
card.fires_on: A subject word (what, which, he, it, that) in historical narrative, just before a past-tense verb like 'would', 'could', 'was to' or 'became'. It often follows 'so that' or a place or thing just introduced.

modes.label: Relative word before 'was to become'
modes.description: 'what', 'which' or 'that' refers back to a thing founded or built, and is followed by a verb telling its later fate.
modes.example: King Stephen himself laid the cornerstone for<< what>> was to become one of the most magnificent

modes.label: 'He' after 'so that'
modes.description: A pronoun starts a purpose clause about a person in history, followed by 'could'.
modes.example: He then spent half of each year in France so that<< he>> could be near her grave.

card.writes: It promotes past-tense verbs such as would, got, began and became, and suppresses the future 'will'.
card.plain: It fires on the subject word in a history passage when the next word is likely 'would', 'could' or 'became'.
